visual: Architectural evergreen with long, narrow, sword-shaped leaves forming bold upright rosettes; mature plants can develop a palm-like trunk.
water: Moderate while establishing; water during prolonged dry spells and keep container plants more consistently watered.
soilWarning: No wet or waterlogged soil in winter
prune: Usually needs little pruning; remove dead or damaged leaves and cut out frost-damaged growth in spring.
hardinessNote: −10 to −5°C · best in a sheltered position; young and container-grown plants are more frost-sensitive.
resilience: Good wind and coastal tolerance once established; moderate drought tolerance.
uses: Architectural planting, patio containers, exotic gardens, coastal gardens, specimen planting.
uncertain: The label text 'idéal en pot et bac' describes suitability for containers and does not identify a cultivar.
Cordyline australis is the most likely identification from the supplied label wording, but the cultivar cannot be confirmed without additional label text or a photo.

visual: Robust evergreen shrub with dark green leaves and loose trusses of white funnel-shaped flowers opening from mauve-tinged buds.
water: Keep evenly moist, particularly while establishing and during dry spring and summer weather.
soilWarning: No lime or chalk; no prolonged waterlogging
prune: Little pruning required; remove dead wood and spent flower trusses after flowering if needed.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten; all parts should be treated as potentially toxic.
resilience: Robust and cold-hardy; benefits from shelter from drying winds.
uses: Woodland gardens, shrub borders, screening, informal hedging, acid-soil planting.

visual: Deciduous maple with deeply lobed green leaves developing strong yellow, orange and red autumn colour.
water: Moderate; maintain even moisture during establishment and dry weather.
soilWarning: No waterlogging, exposure or hot dry sites
prune: Minimal pruning; remove unwanted or damaged branches while dormant, preferably from late autumn to midwinter.
hardinessNote: −20 to −15°C · generally hardy throughout the UK when established.
resilience: Cold-hardy but fine foliage benefits from protection from strong drying winds.
uses: Specimen tree, woodland garden, Japanese-style garden, mixed borders.
uncertain: Acer palmatum var. coreanum is treated by Kew as a synonym of Acer palmatum subsp. amoenum.
The horticultural name Acer palmatum 'Koreanum' has also been associated with 'Korean Gem'; the supplied label does not include 'Korean Gem', so it has not been assumed here.

visual: Upright dissected Japanese maple with finely cut light-green foliage turning vivid yellow, orange and red in autumn.
water: Moderate; keep evenly moist during establishment and water during hot, dry weather.
soilWarning: No waterlogging; shelter from drying winds
prune: Minimal pruning; remove damaged or crossing growth while dormant.
resilience: Good cold tolerance; requires some shelter from drying winds for best foliage.
uses: Specimen shrub or small tree, Japanese gardens, courtyard gardens, mixed borders, large containers.

visual: Vigorous apple tree producing medium to large irregular apples with yellow skin strongly flushed dark red and firm, coarse-textured flesh.
water: Moderate; water well while establishing and during prolonged drought, particularly while fruit is developing.
soilWarning: No waterlogging, shallow chalk or acid soil
prune: Prune according to rootstock and training form; winter-prune standard trees and summer-prune trained forms as appropriate.
toxicity: Fruit flesh is edible; seeds should not be deliberately eaten in quantity.
resilience: Very cold-hardy and vigorous; suited to cooler growing areas.
uses: Edible garden, orchard, wildlife garden, cottage garden, trained fruit tree.
uncertain: Ultimate dimensions depend strongly on the rootstock and training system.
The multilingual label 'Boskoop Rouge' corresponds to Red Belle de Boskoop / Red Boskoop.

visual: Rounded deciduous tree with dark red-purple foliage and masses of pale pink flowers fading toward white in early spring.
water: Moderate while establishing; relatively tolerant once established.
prune: Prune only when necessary, preferably in midsummer to reduce the risk of silver leaf disease.
toxicity: Ripe plum-like fruit may be edible; leaves, stems and kernels contain cyanogenic compounds and should not be eaten.
resilience: Tolerates exposure and a wide range of soils once established.
uses: Specimen tree, avenue planting, wildlife garden, ornamental flowering tree.
uncertain: Prunus cerasifera 'Pissardii' is commonly used in horticulture; RHS currently lists Prunus pissardii and gives Prunus cerasifera 'Atropurpurea' as a synonym.

visual: Compact clump-forming succulent perennial producing fleshy foliage and broad heads of rosy-pink flowers in late summer and autumn.
water: Low; water while establishing then allow the soil to dry between watering.
soilWarning: No wet or heavy soil, above all in winter
prune: Leave dried flower heads for winter structure if desired, then cut old stems to ground level in early spring.
hardinessNote: At least −20 to −15°C · fully hardy in normal UK conditions.
resilience: Excellent drought tolerance once established and generally easy-care.
uses: Sunny borders, gravel gardens, pollinator planting, containers, low-maintenance schemes.
uncertain: The additional label word 'Improved' could not be verified as part of the registered cultivar name, so the plant is treated as Sedum 'Surrender Rose'.
Published retailer information inconsistently describes its hardiness as H6 and H7; H6 is used conservatively here.

visual: Compact evergreen spurge with brilliant yellow spring foliage becoming yellow-green in summer, rusty-orange autumn tips and yellow-green flowers with red nectaries.
water: Moderate while establishing; relatively drought tolerant afterwards.
soilWarning: Sharp drainage; no heavy wet winter soil
prune: Minimal pruning; remove spent flower stems and damaged growth while wearing gloves.
toxicity: Milky sap is toxic if ingested and can strongly irritate skin and eyes; wear gloves when handling.
hardinessNote: −15 to −10°C · generally hardy in most UK gardens with good drainage.
resilience: Drought tolerant once established and naturally compact.
uses: Containers, front of borders, gravel gardens, Mediterranean-style planting, foliage contrast.

visual: Compact evergreen mound of exceptionally dark chocolate-black leaves topped by sprays of vivid cherry-red flowers in summer.
water: Moderate; maintain moisture without allowing the crown to sit wet.
soilWarning: Crown must drain, especially in winter
prune: Remove faded flower spikes and tidy damaged foliage in early spring.
resilience: Cold-hardy and compact; established plants cope with short dry periods.
uses: Containers, edging, ground cover, mixed borders, underplanting, foliage contrast.

visual: Compact clump-forming foliage perennial grown primarily for colourful rounded, lobed leaves and delicate summer flower spikes.
water: Moderate; keep moist but never waterlogged.
soilWarning: No winter waterlogging around the crown
prune: Remove spent flower stems and damaged old foliage; divide and replant ageing clumps when necessary.
hardinessNote: −20 to −15°C · rating inferred from comparable hardy Heuchera cultivars.
resilience: Generally cold-hardy but susceptible to crown problems in persistently wet soil.
uses: Containers, edging, ground cover, borders, underplanting.
uncertain: A reliable cultivar record for Heuchera 'Winterberry' could not be verified.
Dimensions, hardiness and cultivation data therefore use conservative Heuchera-level values rather than invented cultivar-specific claims.
A photograph of the original label would help confirm whether 'Winterberry' is the cultivar name or OCR from another name.

visual: Compact mound of ruffled cranberry-red to purple-red foliage with delicate upright sprays of small pale to white flowers in summer.
water: Moderate; keep evenly moist while avoiding saturated soil.
soilWarning: No winter wet; never let the roots dry out
prune: Remove faded flower spikes and damaged foliage; divide and replant older clumps every few years.
resilience: Cold-hardy; established plants have some drought tolerance but colour and vigour are best with reliable moisture.
uses: Containers, borders, edging, underplanting, ground cover, shade gardens.
uncertain: Some retail labels use 'Indian Summer Cranberry' as though it were the cultivar name; RHS records the trade designation Cranberry with cultivar code 'Ifhepr' in the Indian Summer Series.

visual: Low, spreading hardy geranium forming a mound of deeply lobed green foliage and masses of pale pink cup-shaped flowers marked with darker veins.
water: Moderate while establishing; water during prolonged dry spells.
prune: Remove flowered stems and tired foliage to stimulate fresh leaves and repeat flowering.
resilience: Very cold-hardy and tolerant of a broad range of normal garden soils.
uses: Ground cover, border fronts, rose underplanting, cottage gardens, containers.

visual: Dense evergreen shrub with leathery dark-green leaves edged in bright yellow, silvery undersides and small highly fragrant white autumn flowers.
water: Moderate while establishing; drought tolerant once mature.
soilWarning: No waterlogging; yellows on shallow chalk
prune: Trim after flowering or in late spring to control size; remove any reverted plain-green shoots from variegated plants.
hardinessNote: −15 to −10°C · hardy in most UK gardens.
resilience: Very tolerant of wind, coastal exposure, dry soil and urban conditions once established.
uses: Hedging, screening, coastal gardens, mixed borders, evergreen structure.
uncertain: Frequently sold as Elaeagnus × ebbingei 'Viveleg'; RHS currently places it under Elaeagnus × submacrophylla.

visual: Dense upright evergreen shrub producing glossy cherry-red young foliage that matures dark green, followed by clusters of small white spring flowers.
water: Moderate while establishing; water during prolonged drought and more regularly when container-grown.
soilWarning: No wet, heavy or compacted ground
prune: Responds well to clipping; trim after the spring flush and again later in summer if fresh red growth is desired.
hardinessNote: About −15 to −10°C · generally hardy in most UK gardens, with shelter useful in colder sites.
resilience: Dense, robust evergreen with good pruning tolerance and reasonable drought tolerance after establishment.
uses: Hedging, screening, specimen shrub, mixed borders, topiary, large containers.
uncertain: The supplied OCR 'carrray rouge' has been corrected to the established cultivar name 'Carré Rouge'.

visual: Evergreen oleaster with leathery variegated foliage featuring a soft yellow to creamy-yellow centre and contrasting green margins, plus fragrant autumn flowers.
water: Moderate while establishing; drought tolerant once mature.
soilWarning: No waterlogging; yellows on shallow chalk
prune: Trim after flowering or in spring to maintain shape; remove reverted plain-green shoots promptly.
hardinessNote: −15 to −10°C · hardiness inferred from the parent hybrid and established UK cultivation.
resilience: Good drought, wind and coastal tolerance once established.
uses: Evergreen hedging, screening, mixed borders, coastal planting, foliage contrast.
uncertain: RHS currently records the name Elaeagnus × submacrophylla 'Moonlight' but lists its name status as unresolved.
The word 'ERWIAM' from the supplied text has not been included as part of the cultivar name.

visual: Compact evergreen Japanese spindle with glossy variegated foliage; fresh growth emerges conspicuously creamy-white before developing stronger green coloration.
water: Moderate while establishing; established shrubs tolerate short dry periods.
prune: Trim in late winter or spring if required to maintain a compact form; remove reverted shoots if they occur.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten, particularly fruits and seeds.
hardinessNote: Around −15 to −10°C · suitable for most UK gardens.
resilience: Robust evergreen that tolerates regular clipping and urban conditions.
uses: Low hedging, borders, evergreen structure, containers, compact screening.
uncertain: Reliable cultivar-specific information is relatively limited; mature spread and some care scores are conservative estimates.
The supplied trailing word 'Sense' was not found as part of the cultivar name and has been treated as label/OCR noise.
